title.narrative: Reviving Livelihoods and Enhancing Food Access for Vulnerable Communities in Beletweyne District, Somalia

description.narrative: ltpgtDaryeel Bulsho Guud (DBG) proposes a six-month emergency food security intervention to restore livelihoods and improve food access for vulnerable communities in Beletweyne District, Hiran Region, Somalia. The project aims to improve food access and protect livelihoods for 1,900 vulnerable displaced and rural households (including 2,736 men, 5,472 women, 1,596 boys, and 1,596 girls) in Beletweyne District of Hiraan Region through unconditional cash transfers and agricultural inputs that sustain consumption, restore assets, and build resilience.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe intervention will be implemented in two IDP settlements and two rural villages: Doomeey IDP, Barwaqo IDP, Shabelow, and Qoqane villages. It contributes to the Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF) Strategic Objectives 1 and 2, using a dual-track approach designed to address immediate food needs while supporting early recovery and resilience:ltbrgta) Unconditional Cash Transfers (UCTs):ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtDBG will provide 1,000 vulnerable households with UCTs of $55 per month for three months (totaling $165 per household) during the lean season months of October to December 2025. This transfer aligns with the Food Security Cluster (FSC) and SHF revised transfer value, covering 70% of the Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB).ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtb) Cash+ Agricultural Input Support:ltbrgtA total of 900 riverine households will receive the same UCT value of $165 (over three months), combined with a one-time agricultural input package valued at $130.4 per household. The package includes:ltbrgt ltbrgti.10 kg of maize seedsltbrgtii. 10kg of cowpeas ltbrgtiii. 240grams of assorted vegetable seeds ltbrgtiv. Basic farm tools (hoe and forked hoe)ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis activity will be implemented in October 2025, in alignment with the seasonal cropping calendar and FSNAU guidelines on seed distribution. It aims to enhance short-cycle food production, restore household assets, and reduce dependency on emergency aid.ltbrgtDBG emphasizes inclusion and protection throughout the project. At least 60% of targeted households will be women-headed, and 15% will include persons with disabilities. The intervention integrates SPHERE standards, protection mainstreaming, and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) mechanisms. Transfers will be conducted via mobile money platforms, and inputs procured locally to support market recovery and ensure transparency.ltbrgtTo assess the impact, a Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) survey will be conducted in late December 2025 to early January 2026, targeting at least 15% of beneficiaries across the focus areas. The survey will evaluate satisfaction with the assistance received in terms of quality, quantity, and relevance.ltbrgtDBG’s established operational presence in Hiraan, strong community relationships, and successful track record with SHF-funded projects position it to deliver this timely, life-saving intervention effectively.ltbrgtlt/pgt
